Package neqsim.process.equipment.reservoir

Class InflowPerformance

java.lang.Object
neqsim.process.equipment.reservoir.InflowPerformance
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable
public class InflowPerformance extends Object implements Serializable
InflowPerformance class - liquid inflow performance relationships (IPR) for oil wells.

The IPR models already available through WellFlow are all gas forms: they work in squared pressures and MSm3/day. An oil well needs the liquid forms, in which the rate is proportional to the pressure drawdown itself rather than to the difference of its square, and in which the rate is a stock-tank liquid volume in Sm3/day. This class supplies those, as a small self-contained calculation object that can be evaluated from either end - rate from pressure, or pressure from rate - and attached to a WellFlow through WellFlow.setInflowPerformance(InflowPerformance).

Models

Liquid inflow performance relationships implemented by this class
Model Relationship Use when
LINEAR q = J (Pr - Pwf) the whole drainage area stays above the bubble point
VOGEL q / qmax = 1 - 0.2 (Pwf/Pr) - 0.8 (Pwf/Pr)², qmax = J Pr / 1.8 the reservoir is at or below the bubble point
COMPOSITE linear above the bubble point, Vogel below it an undersaturated reservoir produced at a drawdown that takes the sandface into two-phase flow - the common case, and the one a linear model flatters
JOSHI_HORIZONTAL composite, with J computed from rock and geometry a horizontal drain whose productivity should follow from permeability, net pay and drain length rather than being assumed

Units

Rates are stock-tank liquid Sm3/day, pressures are bara and the productivity index is Sm3/(day·bar). The Darcy productivity helpers additionally take permeability in mD, lengths in m and viscosity in cP.

Usage


 // An undersaturated reservoir 3.7 bar above its bubble point.
 InflowPerformance ipr = InflowPerformance.composite(200.0, 70.68, 66.94);

 double pwf = ipr.bottomHolePressure(2500.0); // bara required for 2500 Sm3/day
 double rate = ipr.rate(55.0); // Sm3/day at 55 bara
 double aof = ipr.absoluteOpenFlow(); // Sm3/day at zero bottom-hole pressure

A horizontal drain whose productivity index is derived rather than assumed: 


 InflowPerformance horizontal = InflowPerformance.joshiHorizontal(2000.0, // permeability, mD
     45.0, // net pay, m
     1500.0, // drain length, m
     800.0, // drainage radius, m
     0.108, // wellbore radius, m
     3.0, // oil viscosity, cP
     1.1224, // formation volume factor
     0.3, // kv / kh
     2.0, // skin
     70.68, // reservoir pressure, bara
     66.94); // bubble point pressure, bara

      public static InflowPerformance joshiHorizontal(double permeabilityMilliDarcy, double netPayMetre, double drainLengthMetre, double drainageRadiusMetre, double wellboreRadiusMetre, double viscosityCentiPoise, double formationVolumeFactor, double kvOverKh, double skin, double reservoirPressure, double bubblePointPressure)
      Create a composite inflow relationship whose productivity index comes from Joshi's horizontal well solution rather than being assumed.
      Parameters:
      permeabilityMilliDarcy - horizontal permeability in mD, greater than zero
      netPayMetre - net pay thickness in m, greater than zero
      drainLengthMetre - horizontal drain length in m, greater than zero
      drainageRadiusMetre - drainage radius in m, greater than zero
      wellboreRadiusMetre - wellbore radius in m, greater than zero
      viscosityCentiPoise - oil viscosity at reservoir conditions in cP, greater than zero
      formationVolumeFactor - oil formation volume factor in rm3/Sm3, greater than zero
      kvOverKh - ratio of vertical to horizontal permeability, greater than zero and normally between 0.01 and 1
      skin - completion skin, dimensionless, zero or greater for a damaged completion
      reservoirPressure - average reservoir pressure in bara, greater than zero
      bubblePointPressure - bubble point pressure in bara, zero or greater
      Returns:
      a composite inflow performance object carrying the derived productivity index

    • joshiProductivityIndex

      public static double joshiProductivityIndex(double permeabilityMilliDarcy, double netPayMetre, double drainLengthMetre, double drainageRadiusMetre, double wellboreRadiusMetre, double viscosityCentiPoise, double formationVolumeFactor, double kvOverKh, double skin)
      Joshi's productivity index for a horizontal well in a bounded drainage ellipse.

      J = 2 π k h / (μ B [ln((a + sqrt(a² - (L/2)²)) / (L/2)) + (β h / L) ln(h / (2 rw)) + S]), with a the half major axis of the drainage ellipse and β = sqrt(kh/kv) the anisotropy. For a thin reservoir column the vertical permeability term dominates the denominator, so kv/kh is the assumption to challenge before the drain length.

      Parameters:
      permeabilityMilliDarcy - horizontal permeability in mD, greater than zero
      netPayMetre - net pay thickness in m, greater than zero
      drainLengthMetre - horizontal drain length in m, greater than zero
      drainageRadiusMetre - drainage radius in m, greater than zero
      wellboreRadiusMetre - wellbore radius in m, greater than zero
      viscosityCentiPoise - oil viscosity in cP, greater than zero
      formationVolumeFactor - oil formation volume factor in rm3/Sm3, greater than zero
      kvOverKh - ratio of vertical to horizontal permeability, greater than zero
      skin - completion skin, dimensionless
      Returns:
      productivity index in Sm3/(day.bar)
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if any dimension, property or permeability is not positive

    • radialProductivityIndex

      public static double radialProductivityIndex(double permeabilityMilliDarcy, double netPayMetre, double drainageRadiusMetre, double wellboreRadiusMetre, double viscosityCentiPoise, double formationVolumeFactor, double skin)
      Steady-state radial Darcy productivity index for a vertical well.

      Useful as a sanity check on an assumed productivity index: if the assumed value and this one differ by more than a factor of two, one of them is describing a different well.

      Parameters:
      permeabilityMilliDarcy - permeability in mD, greater than zero
      netPayMetre - net pay thickness in m, greater than zero
      drainageRadiusMetre - drainage radius in m, greater than the wellbore radius
      wellboreRadiusMetre - wellbore radius in m, greater than zero
      viscosityCentiPoise - oil viscosity in cP, greater than zero
      formationVolumeFactor - oil formation volume factor in rm3/Sm3, greater than zero
      skin - completion skin, dimensionless
      Returns:
      productivity index in Sm3/(day.bar)
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if any dimension or property is not positive, or if the drainage radius is not larger than the wellbore radius
